summary: I develop AI and backend systems that find evidence in documents and videos to answer questions. I implement AI features with Python and PyTorch and connect them to web services with FastAPI and Spring Boot.

My graduate research covers choosing retrieval methods for each question and deciding whether video evidence is sufficient to answer. I led research design, implementation, comparative experiments, and manuscript writing. I am the first author of one published KCI journal paper and one domestic conference paper; a separate IEEE Access manuscript is under review.

Across three paid internships at Kakao and Tilonsoft, I developed AI features and web/backend functionality. In undergraduate team projects, I led ideation, core development, and coordination. I am an M.S. student in Computer Engineering at Jeju National University, expecting to graduate in March 2027.

smartfarm-rag.name: Query-adaptive Retrieval and SmartFarm Operations Support
smartfarm-rag.desc: Developed question-adaptive document retrieval for AI question answering, with a related KCI journal publication.
smartfarm-rag.body:
Developed question-adaptive document retrieval for AI question answering, with a related KCI journal publication.


## My role


Designed the research method, implemented the AI functionality, compared it with existing approaches, and wrote the first-author paper.


## What I built


Combined keyword, semantic, and relationship-based retrieval, selecting a suitable combination for each question. Connecting retrieved documents to AI-generated answers is known as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).


Used prior comparisons of retrieval combinations to replace an additional AI call for choosing retrieval weights.


## Results and evaluation scope


Evidence: One related KCI journal publication


Compared retrieval methods on public data.


A separate SmartFarm operations system connects observations, document evidence, AI explanations, operator approval, and execution-result checks. This operational flow was validated in simulation.


## Technologies


Python · RAG · FastAPI. The research source repository is private.

mv-evirag.name: Selective Response for Multi-View Video Question Answering
mv-evirag.desc: Question answering across multiple camera views involves choosing an input, deciding whether to answer or abstain, and deciding whether to release the generated response. This research separates these decisions and trains answer/abstention behavior using the information available in the input.
mv-evirag.metric: Under review at IEEE Access · submitted August 2026 · First author
mv-evirag.body:
Question answering across multiple camera views involves choosing an input, deciding whether to answer or abstain, and deciding whether to release the generated response. This research separates these decisions and trains answer/abstention behavior using the information available in the input.


## My role


Led research design, model training and implementation, comparative experiments, and first-author writing.


## View selection and response decisions


A relevant person may appear in a video while the region needed to judge an action is occluded. Input selection and answerability were therefore treated as different decisions, using the information available at each stage.


The answerer was trained on both evidence-bearing and evidence-deficient inputs. Response confidence was then used to decide whether to release a generated answer.


## Evaluation and publication


Evaluated answer coverage alongside incorrect responses, managed experimental procedures and model outputs, and reported the comparisons in the manuscript.


Evidence: Under review at IEEE Access · submitted August 2026 · First author


Paper title: Role-Separated Selective Response for Question Answering in Multi-View Video Surveillance


## Technologies


Implemented training and evaluation with Python, PyTorch, and LoRA. The evaluation used supplied regions of interest and rule-defined evidence availability.

rag-evaluation.title: RAG Evaluation Notes
rag-evaluation.summary: A practical evaluation lens for comparing RAG systems across retrieval quality, answer grounding, and operating cost.
rag-evaluation.body:
A practical evaluation lens for comparing RAG systems across retrieval quality, answer grounding, and operating cost.


## Why Evaluation Comes First


If you only look at answer quality in a RAG system, it is easy to miss the cause of failure. The retrieval, reranking, and generation stages need to be separated so you can see whether documents were missed, pushed down, or ignored during answer generation.


## Basic Metrics

- Recall@5: checks whether the supporting evidence appears in the top five retrieved documents.
- MRR: measures how early the first useful evidence appears.
- Groundedness: checks whether the answer is actually supported by retrieved documents.
